full_caption: Evanthe Yarborough, Appellant, v. Larkspur Hill Land & Timber Co., Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: The Cobbleton County Redevelopment Authority condemned 24.0 acres owned by Larkspur Hill Land & Timber Co. at 2660 Ferndale Road, Cobbleton, SB for construction of a veterinary clinic. The sole issue on appeal is the measure of just compensation.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Business losses are not compensable as such. Loss of goodwill is recoverable only where a statute so provides; this State's statute permits recovery of relocation expenses of $640,000 but not lost profits.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The highest and best use of the property is the use to which it may reasonably be put in the reasonably near future. A use dependent on a rezoning is admissible only on a showing that the rezoning was reasonably probable.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: A taking may be effected without formal proceedings where governmental action substantially deprives the owner of the beneficial use of the land. The 9-month closure of the only access drive states a claim for inverse condemnation.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Public use is satisfied where the taking serves a legitimate public purpose; the transfer of the condemned land to a private developer under an enforceable redevelopment agreement does not defeat that purpose under this State's constitution.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Just compensation is the fair market value of the property taken at the date of taking, measured by the price a willing buyer would pay a willing seller, neither being under compulsion.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Where only part of a parcel is taken, the owner recovers the value of the part taken plus severance damages to the remainder, less any special benefit conferred on the remainder by the project.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Evidence of the price paid by the condemnor for neighboring parcels is generally inadmissible, because such sales are made under the shadow of the condemnation power and are not free-market transactions.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Interest on the award runs from the date of taking to the date of payment at the statutory rate of 5 percent, and is a component of just compensation rather than a matter of legislative grace.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The 'scope of the project' rule excludes from the valuation any increase or decrease in value attributable to the project itself, including value changes flowing from the announcement of the project.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: The trial court excluded testimony valuing the parcel as multifamily residential land. Given the pending comprehensive-plan amendment and three comparable rezonings in the corridor, the probability showing was made and the exclusion was error.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: The judgment is reversed and the cause remanded for a new trial on valuation with the excluded testimony admitted.

sections.heading: RIDER 2 — MEASURE OF JUST COMPENSATION
sections.text: Compensation shall be the fair market value of the part taken, determined as of the date of taking, plus damages to the remainder resulting from the taking and from the construction and use of the project as planned, less the value of any special benefit conferred on the remainder. General benefits shared with the community at large shall not be offset. Value shall be determined with reference to the highest and best use, which may include a use requiring a rezoning where the rezoning is reasonably probable.

sections.heading: RIDER 4 — RELOCATION AND BUSINESS LOSSES
sections.text: The Owner is entitled to actual and reasonable moving expenses, expenses of searching for a replacement site not exceeding $640,000, and reestablishment expenses. Loss of business profits and loss of goodwill are not compensable except to the extent expressly provided by statute. Payment of relocation benefits is not an offset against just compensation.

sections.heading: RIDER 5 — INTEREST, POSSESSION AND ABANDONMENT
sections.text: Interest at 5 percent per annum accrues on the difference between the deposit and the final award from the date of taking to the date of payment, as a constitutional component of just compensation. The Condemnor may take possession upon deposit. If the Condemnor abandons the taking before final judgment, it shall pay the Owner's reasonable costs, appraisal fees and attorney's fees actually incurred.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Attorney's Fees
sections.text: In any action to enforce or construe this instrument, the prevailing party shall recover its reasonable attorney's fees, expert fees and costs, at trial and on appeal. Where the instrument grants fees to one party only, this clause shall be read as reciprocal and shall entitle the other party to fees on the same terms if that party prevails.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Waiver and Course of Dealing
sections.text: No waiver of any breach shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party charged. The acceptance of a payment with knowledge of a breach, the failure to insist on strict performance, or any course of dealing between the parties shall not constitute a waiver of that or any subsequent breach, nor estop the party from enforcing the provision thereafter.
